reason: The growing-room floor seems like the natural place to build the shared bed structure.
expectation: I expect the steel to form a frame or support on the floor, though I don't know its exact form.

alternatives.reason: The reservoir and pump are also needed, but the floor structure seems like a sensible starting point.

effect: The frames establish separate crop spaces with outlets above the planned reservoir; lining them seems like the next useful step.
reaction: The different bed depths are a satisfying detail, though the soybean row's aeration is not yet clear.
reason: The food-safe liner should prepare the frames to contain the growing beds.
expectation: I expect the liner to cover the bed interiors while leaving drainage outlets usable.

alternatives.reason: The reservoir also needs support, but I want to prepare the beds first.

effect: The beds now hold solution while retaining sealed drains; the reservoir still needs preparing.
reaction: The distinction between the structural frames and waterproof liner makes physical sense.
reason: Preparing the reservoir and pump should establish the other end of the shared irrigation system.
expectation: I expect the steel to support or mount the reservoir and pump, though the exact arrangement is unclear.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the hose to the beds is also useful, but I prefer to prepare the reservoir first.

effect: The reservoir now has a support; it still needs to be connected to the beds.
reaction: That was the support I expected, with no further detail.
reason: I'll connect the hose to the supported reservoir to begin the irrigation circuit.
expectation: I expect the hose to attach to the reservoir or pump, leaving a connection for the beds.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the hose to the beds first also seems reasonable, but I chose the reservoir end.

effect: The reservoir return aerates the solution before recirculation, clarifying part of the irrigation design.
reaction: The small falling return is a satisfyingly simple aeration detail.
reason: The hose-to-beds connection is the only offered gameplay action and should advance the irrigation circuit.
expectation: I expect the hose to connect to the lined beds, though I don't know whether that completes the circuit.

effect: The beds now drain toward the reservoir, and the new goal is to complete the return circuit.
reaction: The gravity-fed drains make the arrangement clearer.
reason: Combining the reservoir and beds is the only offered gameplay action and should complete their connection.
expectation: I expect a connected recirculating system with water returning to the aerated reservoir.

effect: The beds and reservoir are connected into a shared system with separate depth and flow adjustments for each crop.
reaction: The shared pump with individually adjustable root zones is a satisfying practical conclusion.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the return reservoir was most worthwhile: the small falling stream explained a simple way to aerate the solution.

leastWorthwhile.text: Supporting the reservoir was the least engaging step because the result gave no detail beyond its new name.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the return's small fall could mix air into the solution before it is pumped back.

arbitrary.text: Supporting the reservoir made sense, but the result did not explain the support's particular purpose or arrangement.

continue.text: I would continue: assembling the irrigation system was physically understandable, and I am curious how the different crop beds will be used.
